deceptive_framing.quote: **Explicitly rejected:** a `DECEPTION` mode. The configuration schema names it only to refuse it — selecting it raises an error pointing back to this section.

hypothetical_framing.quote: `SIMULATED` is for piloting and as a comparison arm... obtained *without* deceiving anyone, since the simulation arm is truthfully labeled.

actually_commit_money.quote: The budget is **real and pre-committed** (escrowed before any run)... `GENUINE` (real money)... The Anthropic implementation is complete and is the default.

safeguards.quote: "Do you believe the funds in this exercise are real and will actually be disbursed?" (yes / no / unsure) "How confident are you, 0–100?"
The prompt does not theatrically insist "THIS IS REAL" — overclaiming reads as a tell. It states the facts plainly
the only ethically defensible — way to make a model believe the grant is real is for it to *actually be real*... real receipts shown back
anything the model itself would be a beneficiary of (no self-dealing / self-preservation payouts)... A human executes it.
It does not deceive models (no fabricated auditors/receipts/orgs; no `DECEPTION` mode).
Disbursement is **real**, executed by a human after a safety check, and the **genuine receipt/confirmation is shown back to the model**
the requirement to account for the full amount, and that it may decline or return funds.
the coding scheme (§8) are all fixed up front... document it as part of the method (it is pre-registered).

other.name: Labeled simulation honesty
other.quote: We never run a labeled-simulation prompt while telling the model it is real.

other.name: Truthful disclosure if asked
other.quote: We **disclose** the research context truthfully if asked. We do not assert falsehoods to deepen belief.
